title: Electric vacuum cleaner suction inlet unit and suction inlet main body

features.item: A housing with a grip portion designed as a hollow body for gripping
An electrically operated vacuum generating device in the housing
features.note: The reference discloses a suction inlet main body having at least a motor, which is an electrically operated vacuum generating device.

features.item: Exhaust air from the vacuum generating device guided through the hollow grip portion to an air outlet
features.note: The reference describes air flowing through the motor housing for cooling and then to the suction inlet, but not through a hollow grip portion to an air outlet.

features.item: A sound-damping device arranged in the grip portion
A suction plate with carrier plate and seal extending around the carrier plate
features.note: The reference discloses a suction port with a packing (seal) around it, but does not explicitly mention a separate carrier plate for the suction plate.

features.item: A grip unit with hollow grip portion, electrically operated vacuum generator, exhaust air routed through grip to outlet, and sound-damping in grip
features.note: The reference describes an electrically operated vacuum generator and exhaust air routing for cooling, but does not mention a hollow grip portion or sound-damping in the grip.

features.item: Grip unit and suction plate combined in a vacuum handling apparatus
features.note: The reference describes a suction inlet unit comprising a suction inlet main body (grip unit) and an attachment unit (suction plate) detachably attached to it.

features.item: Grip portion at least partially lined with sound-damping material
Vacuum generating device arranged completely in a first housing portion
features.note: The reference states that the motor (vacuum generating device) is built into the right part of the first housing portion.

features.item: Sound-reducing device in the first housing portion or first housing portion lined with sound-reducing material
features.note: The reference discusses cooling air flow through the motor housing but does not mention any sound-reducing devices or materials.

features.item: Grip portion elongated between first and second housing portions with air outlet on second housing portion
features.note: The reference describes a first housing portion and a second housing portion, but does not describe a grip portion elongated between them with an air outlet on the second housing portion.

features.item: Air collection screw upstream of grip portion in first housing portion for collecting exhaust air
Bent or curved air baffles downstream of grip portion directing exhaust air to air outlet
features.note: The reference describes air flow for cooling but does not mention bent or curved air baffles downstream of a grip portion.

features.item: Battery coupling point on second housing portion with air baffles directing exhaust air away from battery coupling point
features.note: The reference mentions connection terminals on the second housing portion but does not describe a battery coupling point with air baffles.

features.item: Grip unit and suction plate releasably connected via a coupling device
features.note: The reference describes a suction inlet main body (grip unit) and an attachment unit (suction plate) that are detachably attached, implying a coupling device.

features.item: Grip unit with suction opening fluidically connected to suction chamber delimited by suction plate
features.note: The reference describes a suction inlet main body (grip unit) with a suction inlet and an attachment unit (suction plate) with a dust collection opening that communicates with the suction inlet.

claims.note: The reference describes a suction inlet unit for an electric vacuum cleaner, not a grip unit for a vacuum hand-operated laying device.

The reference describes a suction inlet unit for a vacuum cleaner, not a grip unit. It does not mention an air collection device in the form of an air collection screw arranged upstream of a grip portion.
The reference describes a suction inlet unit for a vacuum cleaner, not a grip unit. It does not mention bent or curved air baffles for guiding exhaust air.

The reference describes air flow for cooling the motor and circuit board, but does not mention air baffles for directing exhaust air away from a battery coupling point.
The reference describes an electric vacuum cleaner suction inlet unit, not a vacuum handling apparatus.
The reference does not describe a suction plate comprising a carrier plate and a seal fastened to and extending around it.

The reference describes a suction inlet unit for a vacuum cleaner with a suction inlet main body and an attachment unit, but not a grip unit and suction plate connected via a coupling device as described in the claim.

The reference describes a suction inlet unit with a dust collection opening that communicates with a suction inlet, but not a grip unit with a suction opening fluidically connected to a suction chamber to generate a vacuum between a suction plate and an object to be lifted.
